record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.original_question: Characterize all complex-valued multiplicative sequences a=(a_n)_{n\ge 1}, meaning a_{mn}=a_m a_n for all positive integers m,n, for which there exists a nontrivial continuous function φ:R→C satisfying the replicative system (1/n) Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} φ((x+k)/n) = a_n φ(x) for every real x and every positive integer n.

evidence.quote: We finish this replicativity part with a problem posed by H.-H. Kairies [138] (cf. also [135]). Characterize those complex sequences a satisfying am·n = am · an for m, n ∈ N for which there exists a non-trivial continuous function ϕ : R → C such that 1/n Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} ϕ((x + k)/n) = anϕ(x) holds for all x ∈ R and n ∈ N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A complex-valued sequence $a=(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is called multiplicative if $a_{mn}=a_m a_n$ for all positive integers $m,n$. Given such a sequence, consider the replicative system of functional equations
$$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\varphi\!\left(\frac{x+k}{n}\right)=a_n\,\varphi(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R},\ n\in\mathbb{N},$$
for an unknown continuous function $\varphi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$. Characterize precisely those multiplicative sequences $a=(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ for which this system admits a nontrivial (i.e., not identically zero) continuous solution $\varphi$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, originally posed by H.-H. Kairies, asks for a full characterization of multiplicative sequences admitting nontrivial continuous replicative solutions. Available literature (Kairies, "Replicativity and Function Spaces", 2000; "Functional equations for peculiar functions", 1997) studies connections between the regularity class of solutions and the magnitude of the multiplicative coefficient sequence, but does not give a complete characterization. No subsequent result resolving the problem in full was found.
